title: Pizza al Taglio
subtitle: Roman sheet-pan pizza sold by the slice
excerpt: Pizza al taglio is a thick-rimmed Roman pizza baked in a rectangular tin and sold by weight. The dough is highly hydrated and very airy inside with a crisp base. It can be topped simply with tomato and mozzarella or with any combination you like.
sourceNotes: Pizza al taglio (pizza by the cut) is the Roman bakery tradition of baking pizza in long rectangular trays and selling it in lengths cut with scissors. The style is distinct from Neapolitan pizza: the dough is much higher in hydration, the crumb is more open, and the pizza is never paper-thin. The technique was developed in Roman bakeries after World War II and has been popularised internationally by bakers such as Gabriele Bonci (Pizzarium, Rome).

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 tray, about 30 x 40 cm, serving 6 as a snack
recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cut slices individually. Reheat at 200°C for 10 to 12 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough ferments in the fridge overnight. Shape and top on baking day.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional. Preheat the tin in the oven before adding the dough.

content.text: Pizza al taglio is Roman bakery pizza: baked in a large tin, cut into rectangles with scissors, and sold by weight. The dough is wetter than Neapolitan pizza dough and ferments overnight to develop a very open, airy crumb. The base crisps against the hot, oiled tin while the inside stays soft. Topped here with tomato and mozzarella, though the topping is flexible.

Combine the flour, yeast, and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Mix well with a spoon or your hand for 3 to 4 minutes until a wet, sticky dough forms. It will not knead like a standard dough.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 1 hour, then refrigerate overnight.
Oil a large rectangular tin generously. Heat the oven to 240°C with the tin inside.

Take the dough out of the fridge and leave at room temperature for 30 minutes. Tip it into the hot oiled tin and press out with oiled fingers to fill the tin. If it resists, leave for 10 minutes and try again.

Spread the passata over the dough and scatter the mozzarella. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden on top and the base is crisp when you lift a corner. Cool for 5 minutes before cutting.

Pizza al taglio is the most practical version of pizza for home baking because the dough fits a standard baking tin and the high hydration makes it forgiving to handle. Roman bakeries sell it all day from large trays in the window, cutting pieces to order with scissors. The topping can be varied: try potato and rosemary, artichoke and pecorino, or just good olive oil and sea salt.
